title: The Night Nothing Is Sold
logline: For one full-moon night an inland junction town turns its entire apparatus of appetite around: the same roads, the same cooking on the same scale, the same queues, and at the end of every one of them somebody hands food to a stranger and takes nothing for it.
human_question: Is the drive that makes people want things a different drive from the one that makes them give things away, or is it the same drive pointed somewhere else?

place.what_kind_of_place: A mid-sized working town where several main roads meet, built around a lake and overlooked by a line of bare rock outcrops, the largest of them standing three hundred metres straight up over the streets. For most of the year it is a place goods pass through. On two full-moon nights it becomes something else. Committees form around temples, workplaces, sports clubs and single streets; families pool money; farmers send vegetables; bamboo frames and tarpaulins go up along the main roads; and volunteers chop, cook and serve through the night. Nothing in any of those sheds is for sale. Vehicles are flagged down and fed, queues form on the pavement, and the town runs on cooked rice, herbal porridge, sweet drinks and tea until whatever there is runs out.
place.why_it_is_worth_watching: Three things carry it with the sound off. From the air, an ordinary provincial road system lit end to end with temporary sheds, traffic slowed to walking pace between them, and the lake holding the reflection of the lanterns and the lit structures. At ground level, the cooking, which is industrial in scale and entirely domestic in method: sacks of rice, vats over gas and firewood, forty hands on one chopping bench, an assembly line of plates. And the giving itself, filmed close and without commentary: a cup passed through a car window, a plate handed to somebody who does not say anything, a queue moving at the speed of one ladle.
place.what_moves_or_changes: The night has its own arc and nobody controls it. Frames go up through the afternoon. The first food is ready around dusk. The roads thicken and the queues get long, and there is a point late on when a shed runs out and stops. After midnight the servers are running on nothing, the crowds thin, and the last of it goes to whoever is still walking. Before dawn the tarpaulins come down, the road is hosed, and what is left on the ground is eaten by the town's crows and dogs, who have learned the date.
place.when_it_looks_best: The full-moon nights of May and June, and the day after each, which is when the roads are lined. The working hours are from about seven in the evening until the food is gone, with the densest crowds before midnight and the best light for the aerial work in the first hour of darkness. The final beat needs the hour before sunrise, when the street is empty and still wet.

two_layers.without_the_philosophy: A night film about a town on a festival night: bamboo going up in the afternoon, lanterns, lit structures, steam, forty people cooking for ten thousand, strangers fed on a highway, and an empty wet road at dawn. It has its own shape, from an empty street to an empty street, and its own suspense, which is whether the food lasts. A viewer who never hears a word of the narration gets a complete night, a real civic machine, and a piece of generosity at a scale most people have never seen.
two_layers.with_the_philosophy: The same footage becomes the group's correction of itself. The voice points out that the books this series is reading do not treat wanting as automatically a fault: they separate the wish to do something from the sticking that makes it grasping, and they say the wish takes the colour of whatever it serves. Then it points at the road, where every part of the machinery of appetite is running at full stretch with the arrow turned outward. It is careful not to sanctify anybody, because the sources classify a moment of mind, not a person, and nothing on this road shows anyone's aim.

sequence.on_screen: Late afternoon from the air: the lake, the rock, five roads meeting, and along them bamboo frames going up and tarpaulins being tied.
sequence.voice: By tonight there will be food on every one of these roads, and none of it will be for sale. The money was collected weeks ago. The vegetables came from people who grew them. What goes up this afternoon comes down again before sunrise.

sequence.on_screen: Inside a kitchen shed at dusk. Sacks of rice, a chopping bench with a dozen people at it, vats, a tally book, a collection box with the lid off.
sequence.voice: The books are careful about what is happening in this room. The wish to do a thing, they say, is not the same as the wanting that sticks to it. It is a working part of any purposeful moment, and it has no colour of its own. Put it in a grasping mind and it strengthens the grasping. Put it in a good one and it works against it.

sequence.on_screen: Full dark on the main road. Vehicles slowed to walking pace, volunteers stepping out with trays, cups handed through windows, a bus emptying.
sequence.voice: This is the line these books actually draw. The same act, they say, is counted by what it is for. Done out of faith, or kindness, or plain sense about what is useful, an ordinary act is not counted a fault at all. And the person eating is doing the thing the books name outright as clear of fault: quieting hunger.

sequence.on_screen: A queue on the pavement, plates coming down the line, people eating standing up, a child asleep against somebody in the line.
sequence.voice: The same book has a long list of the everyday occasions when wanting shows up. Good food is on it. So are clothes, music, earning money, a trip away, and raising your children. It is a description of how much of a day runs on liking and reaching, not a list of crimes. And it counts minds, not people, which is why nothing in this queue can be sorted by looking at it.

sequence.on_screen: Two in the morning. The servers are slow now, the cooks have not eaten, somebody is washing a vat with a hose, and the queue is still there.
sequence.voice: The books describe effort as something mental rather than bodily, and as the thing that does not turn back until the job is finished. They also refuse to call it a virtue. They picture it as a boat on a current: it carries a mind wherever that mind is already leaning, and doing good is described as carrying a load uphill. Nothing about being tired proves anything.

sequence.on_screen: A shed runs out: the bottom of the pot, a hand turning people away with an apology, the frame starting to come down around them. Somebody eats the last of the rice standing up out of the pot.
sequence.voice: One of these books says that the wish to do, trained and made the leading thing in a life, is a base of success and can carry a person all the way to what they are after. Tonight it built a shed on a main road and gave rice to people whose names nobody asked for.

sequence.on_screen: The hour before sunrise. Wet road, flattened cardboard, a stack of tarpaulins, and crows and three dogs working over what is left on the ground. Nobody is watching them.
sequence.voice: There is one small case in these books about exactly this. Feeding an animal because you enjoy watching it eat is counted as one thing, and feeding it as a kindness to the animal is the one case the book comes out and calls wholesome. At this hour there is nobody left here to enjoy anything. The food is just going where food goes.

concept_merge.why_together: Read fresh, C005 is not a list of sins. It sets out the everyday occasions when greed-rooted minds arise, from good food and fine clothes to earning money and raising children, and says frankly that for ordinary people most minds from waking to sleep are of that kind [C005-M:L7]; then it draws its real line by aim, so that the same act done from faith, loving-kindness, compassion or practical sense is not counted unwholesome [C005-M:L9], eating to relieve hunger sits on the clear side [C005-M:L13], and feeding an animal as a kindness to it is the one case in the extract that the source comes out and calls wholesome rather than merely not unwholesome [C005-M:L21]. C021 supplies what an aim is made of. The six occasional factors run through wholesome and unwholesome minds alike and take the colour of the mind they join [C021-P:L25], and both sources insist that desire-to-act is not greed: the wish to take up an object [C021-P:L69], the wish to do [C021-M:L27], lacking greed's stickiness, supporting greed inside a greed-rooted mind and opposing it inside a wholesome one, and developed into a predominant factor and a base of success [C021-P:L75]. Effort is mental rather than bodily and does not turn back until a task is done [C021-M:L19], and is pictured as a boat on a current, carrying a mind wherever it already leans [C021-P:L53]. A night when a whole town's cooking, queuing, carrying and spending is organised so that nothing is sold lets both be filmed rather than argued.
concept_merge.what_it_reveals: That the subject of this group is not appetite but stickiness. C005 on its own sounds, to an ordinary listener, like a verdict on ordinary pleasures, which its own digest says it is not. C021 on its own is a parts list. Put together on this location they produce the one film in the group that shows wanting is not automatically a fault: the same drive, the same organising, the same effort and the same all-night stamina that fill a market fill a free kitchen, and from the roadside the two are indistinguishable. Which is also the film's discipline. It never claims to know why any particular person is out here. It films only the direction the food is moving, and leaves the aim where the sources leave it, out of sight.

concept_links.why: The Margaya's aim line is the film's subject and can be watched here at scale: the same act is not counted unwholesome when it is done from faith, kindness, compassion or a practical sense of what is useful [C005-M:L9], eating to quiet hunger is explicitly clear [C005-M:L13], and the one case the extract calls wholesome outright is feeding an animal as a kindness to it rather than for the pleasure of watching it eat [C005-M:L21], which is what the last beat rests on. The occasions list sits underneath all of it, naming good food, clothes, music, earning and family life as the everyday places wanting shows up [C005-M:L7]. Four limits from the digest are load-bearing and are written into the film rather than left to chance. The source classifies minds and not persons, so no volunteer here is sanctified and nobody in a queue is judged. The digest's own uncertainty is honoured too: several of these cases are called only 'not unwholesome' without being told what they are instead [C005-M:L9] [C005-M:L13], and the film must not quietly upgrade every giver on the road to 'wholesome'. The source does not preach self-denial, and it does not dissolve everything into motive either, since it still names theft, lying and misconduct as courses of harm carried out through wanting [C005-M:L3]. Finally, its remark that most of an ordinary day runs on greed-rooted minds [C005-M:L7] is the author's unquantified general statement and is never put to a viewer as a measurement.

This is where the group first sees a wanting that the sources refuse to call greed. Both texts define desire-to-act as the wish to take up or to do [C021-P:L69] [C021-M:L27], insist it lacks greed's stickiness, and say it follows the moral side of whatever mind it joins, strengthening greed in one and opposing it in another; the Pradeepika adds that developed it becomes a predominant factor and a base of success [C021-P:L75]. Effort is defined as mental rather than bodily and as what does not turn back until a task is done [C021-M:L19], which is what an all-night kitchen is made of, and the six occasional factors are stated to run across wholesome and unwholesome minds alike, taking the colour of the mind they join [C021-P:L25]. The digest's guards are the reason this can be in the film at all without becoming a motivational reading. 'Follow your passion' is ruled out, because the same wish inside a greed-rooted mind strengthens the greed. 'Hard work is always virtuous' is ruled out by the boat on the current, which carries a mind downhill as easily as up [C021-P:L53]; this is why the two-in-the-morning beat refuses to treat exhaustion as proof of goodness. The traditional physiology of rapture moving the body [C021-P:L61] is not used, and the digest's note that the decision factor is firm while often wrong [C021-P:L45] is a reason the film does not treat anyone's conviction as evidence.

what_the_viewer_could_understand: That the wish to do something is not the same as the wanting that sticks, that these books say so directly, and that an entire town can run the whole machinery of appetite for a night with the arrow pointing outward. And that nobody watching from the roadside, the film included, can tell what any one person out here was after.
what_must_be_real: The committees' own money, their own food and their own hours. No stall funded, prompted, scheduled or scaled up by the production, because the moment the film pays for the giving it is filming itself. Nobody asked to serve or to receive for the camera, no handover restaged, no queue re-formed, and no one filmed eating who does not want to be. The animals in the last beat are filmed as found, never baited, fed or moved for the shot, and no animal's condition is dramatised.
position_hint: middle to late in the group: it only does its work once the group has shown wanting at its widest, because its whole job is to refuse the conclusion the earlier films invite. No location reasoning is involved.
risks: Sanctifying the givers. The sources classify a moment of mind, not a person, and the digest notes that most of these cases are called only 'not unwholesome' rather than wholesome [C005-M:L9].
Shaming anyone who takes food, takes a lot of it, or gives nothing; the film has no interest in who deserves what.
Filming an act of merit as a performance, or a religious observance as spectacle.
Reading 'only intentions matter' into the source, which still names particular actions as courses of harm [C005-M:L3].
Drifting into 'hard work is virtuous' or 'follow your passion'; the sources hold effort and the wish to do as morally colourless [C021-P:L53].
Preaching self-denial by implication, when the source allows wealth earned and spent wisely.
Turning the film into the adjacent stories that are real but are not this one: waste, hygiene, traffic, or the cost to the families who pay for it.
Consent in a crowd, at night, with people filmed while eating, and with children present in queues.
Making a viewer of another faith, or of none, feel the film is preaching at them; the voice describes what a book says and never recommends.
Drone flight over dense night crowds and a lit main road, which may be refused outright.
drop_if: Access can only be had by funding, organising or scheduling a stall, which would make the generosity the production's own.
Filming cannot be done without interrupting the serving or blocking the road.
The only material available is an arranged, camera-facing handover rather than the night as it runs.

connections.note: The same work and the same all-night fire, once for a price and once for nothing.
A thing bought in order to be put down and left, and a thing cooked in order to be handed away.

selection.reason: The one film in the group that shows wanting is not automatically a fault, now carried by a standing collective practice instead of by one person's kindness.

review.note: Rewritten into the footage-led shape. Dropped the old situation block, which was built on one person who feeds stray dogs by name and on the passers-by set against them; a film cannot rest on a single protagonist's virtue or on anyone else's casualness. New location: a junction town on the two full-moon nights when its main roads are lined with free food stalls run by committees, so the generosity is a standing collective practice with a physical rhythm rather than one person's routine. The digest's animal case is kept, but at dawn, on what is left in the road, with nobody watching. New title, old title kept in aliases. Both concept links re-tested against their digests and rewritten: C005 re-grounded on the aim line and on the digest's own uncertainty that most of these cases are called only 'not unwholesome'; C021 re-grounded on desire-to-act as the wish to do, on effort as mental and not turning back, and on the boat-on-a-current refusal to treat effort as a virtue. Added place, two_layers, a seven-beat sequence and a proposed location. Connections re-pointed inside the group.

suggested_location.name: Kurunegala

also_known_as.name: Ethagala
also_known_as.meaning: elephant rock, the outcrop that stands over the town

suggested_location.region: Kurunegala District, North Western Province; the junction town where the Colombo, Kandy, Puttalam and Anuradhapura roads meet, at the foot of a line of rock outcrops
suggested_location.why_here: It is named among the towns that run active free-food circuits on the two full-moon festivals, and unlike a pilgrimage centre it is an ordinary working town, so the film watches a practice rather than a monument and the people fed are travellers on through-roads rather than pilgrims who came for it. Four main roads meet here, which means the giving happens on moving traffic and not inside a compound, and that is what makes it filmable as a system: sheds along the carriageway, vehicles slowed, queues on pavements. The geography gives the aerial work everything it needs in one frame, a lake in the middle of the town holding the reflected light and a rock three hundred metres high directly above it to see the whole lit circuit at once. It is also compact enough that the build-up in the afternoon, the peak before midnight and the strike before dawn can all be covered without moving base.
what_to_film: The town from the rock in the last light, with the frames going up along the roads below and the lake beginning to hold the lights.
One kitchen shed from the start: the money box, the tally book, the sacks, the chopping bench with a dozen people at it, the vats going on.
The handover on the road itself, filmed long and close: trays going out to slowed vehicles, cups through windows, and what people do with their faces when they are given something for nothing.
A queue at full length, at the speed it actually moves, including the waiting rather than only the serving.
The scale of the cooking against the scale of the eating: what a hundred kilos of rice looks like going in, and how long it lasts.
The late hours, after midnight, when the volunteers are finished and still serving, and the moment a shed runs out and starts to come down.
The hour before dawn: the wet empty road, the stacked tarpaulins, and the crows and dogs working over what is left, filmed as found and from a distance.
suggested_location.access: By road; the town sits on the main routes north from the capital and west from the hill capital, and is an easy base. Permission is not one permission: each stall is run by its own committee, temple, workplace or street group, and each would have to agree separately. Police and traffic control are involved on festival nights, and any drone work over crowds and a lit main road needs clearance that may not be given.
suggested_location.best_time: The full-moon nights of Vesak in May and Poson in June, and the following night in each case. Serving runs from about dusk until the food is finished, with the heaviest crowds before midnight. The last beat needs the hour before sunrise.

suggested_location.research_note: The practice itself, how stalls are funded and staffed, what is served and the fact that this town is among those running active circuits are from the sources above and are desk research only. The town's coordinates, elevation, lake and the height of the outcrop are from the encyclopaedia entries. Which roads carry the densest circuit, how many stalls run in a given year, whether committees will agree to be filmed, traffic and drone permissions, and whether the dawn material exists as described are all unverified.

unknowns: No committee, stall or permission has been found or confirmed. Everything here is a research direction.
Whether a single night can carry the whole arc, or whether the film needs both festivals and two different years, is unverified.
Whether the animals at dawn are actually there in the numbers the last beat assumes has not been checked, and the beat is dropped rather than arranged if they are not.
Drone permission over a crowded lit town at night is unverified and may be refused outright.
evidence_class_note: Editorial proposal. The location is Claude's suggestion and awaits Chathura's verdict; its supporting detail is desk research and is unverified. No scene or shot is decided here.
